ledger.reason: R-003 is the only active rule, so there is nothing to merge. It already uses family ranges: office/outpatient E/M 99202-99215 and immunization administration 90460-90474. It does not fire on either denied claim, because neither CLM-012 nor CLM-027 has an immunization administration line. Dropping more conditions would turn the rule into a blanket 'paid' exception that the single paid claim (CLM-017) does not support. Removing the E/M or no-modifier-25 condition would change the policy it describes. The denied claims are CARC 5 (POS mismatch) and CARC 29 (timely filing), which are unrelated causes, so no change is proposed.

There is only one active rule. R-004 (CARC 16 when any line has dx_pointer_count < 1) already states the policy at its most general: it fires on any service line with no diagnosis pointer, regardless of CPT, POS, or plan. It has no code, threshold, or context conditions that could be widened or dropped. The payer=CASCADE condition is the minimal scoping condition. The rule explains CLM-002, where line 84443 has no pointer. It does not fire on paid claims CLM-010 or CLM-018, since every line on both has at least one pointer. No merge or generalization is warranted.

No changes proposed. The three active rules each describe a different policy: timely filing (CARC 29), modifier 59 rejected (CARC 4/N823), and the out-of-network paid exception. Rules with different outcomes or CARCs cannot be merged. Each rule is already minimal, with only a payer condition and one condition that carries the policy. R-006 already fires on any line carrying modifier 59, regardless of CPT, so there is no code family to widen. R-007 keys on in_network=false alone. For R-005 the evidence would allow a timely-filing threshold anywhere between 3 days (latest paid claim) and 204 days (earliest CARC 29 denial). Lowering it from 180 would be speculative and would not cover any additional observed claim, so it is left as is.

Two paid BAYVIEW claims are now available, so the POS 02 and timely filing rules are resubmitted. Both paid claims use POS 11, were submitted within 4 days, are in network and have positive line charges, so none of these rules fires on a paid claim. Timely filing: the cutoff must be above 4 (latest paid) and at or below 105 (only CARC 29 denial). I chose 90, the common Medicaid managed care limit, rather than the minimal 4, to avoid denying ordinary claims. Zero charge (RARC M79) is written as line charge lte 0 so it covers any procedure. Out-of-network is written on in_network alone; the referral on file did not prevent the denial.

ledger.reason: CLM-013 billed vitamin D 25-OH (82306) for fatigue (R5383). It was denied CARC 167 with N115, which indicates the medical necessity test of the vitamin D NCD/LCD failed. I generalized to the vitamin D assay family (82306, 82652) and required that the line point to no diagnosis on the covered list (deficiency, calcium/parathyroid disorders, osteoporosis/osteomalacia, CKD, malabsorption, long-term drug therapy, bariatric surgery or transplant status, sarcoidosis). The covered-diagnosis exclusion is inferred from the standard NCD rather than forced by an observed claim; it keeps the rule from denying covered vitamin D tests on unseen claims. Paid labs (80053 with 36415) use other CPTs, so the rule does not fire on them. The rule also does not fire on CLM-002, which has a separate missing-pointer cause (CARC 16, existing rule).

No replacements proposed. Each active rule covers a different policy: R-003 is the paid exception for E/M billed with immunization admin without modifier 25, R-008 is CARC 5 for POS 02, R-009 is CARC 29 for timely filing, R-010 is CARC 16 for zero-charge lines, and R-011 is CARC 242 for out-of-network. No two rules share a CARC and cause, so there is nothing to merge. The rules are also already as general as their policies. R-008, R-010 and R-011 each have one defining condition plus the payer. R-009's 90-day threshold is the stated filing limit; the evidence alone would allow anything above 4 days (max paid 4, min denied 105), but tightening it to the sparse data would contradict the documented policy. R-003 already uses the full E/M range (99202-99215) and immunization admin range (90460-90474). Its modifier-25 condition defines the exception, and widening an override rule could suppress real denials.

There are only two active rules, and they cover different policies, so they cannot be merged. R-004 (CARC 16, a line with no diagnosis pointer) and R-012 (CARC 167, vitamin D assay with a non-covered diagnosis) have different CARCs and different causes. R-004 is already fully general: payer plus any line with dx_pointer_count < 1. R-012 already names both vitamin D assay codes (82306, 82652), and there is no wider code family to extend it to. Its none_startswith diagnosis condition is the actual cause of the CARC 167 denial (RARC N115, LCD/NCD covered-diagnosis list). No paid claim contains a vitamin D assay, so the replay gate would accept dropping that condition. But doing so would turn a medical-necessity policy into a blanket non-coverage rule and misstate why the payer denies. Neither rule can be safely generalized further on this evidence.

R-014 covered only head/neck CT/MRI (70450-70559), but its stated policy is all advanced imaging. I widened it to an explicit list of CT/MRI codes. A numeric range would have swept in plain x-rays, which need no auth. The list still covers CLM-030 (70551, no auth). It does not fire on paid CLM-028 (72148), because that claim carries a prior auth number. I left R-005, R-006, R-007 and R-013 unchanged. Each is a distinct policy with no merge partner, and each is already as broad as its single condition or code family allows.

ledger.reason: CLM-016 was denied CO-97 with RARC M15, which means separately billed services or tests were bundled. The claim billed the routine venipuncture 36415 alongside the comprehensive metabolic panel 80053. I generalized each side to its code class: venipuncture and specimen collection 36400-36416, and pathology/laboratory 80047-89398. Neither paid Bayview claim (CLM-017 and CLM-022) has a venipuncture line or a lab line, so the rule fires on zero paid claims. I kept the lab-pairing condition because the denial is a bundling denial: CARC 97 requires another service to be included in, not simply the presence of 36415. I added no POS, diagnosis or modifier conditions, since no counterexample forces them.

No replacements proposed. No two rules share both a CARC and a cause, so nothing can be merged. Each rule is already as general as the stated policy allows:
- R-003 already covers the full office E/M range (99202-99215) and the full immunization administration range (90460-90474). Dropping the E/M condition would turn a modifier-25 exception into a blanket 'paid' rule for any claim with immunization admin, which the policy does not support.
- R-008 (POS 02, CARC 5), R-010 (zero-charge line, CARC 16) and R-011 (out-of-network, CARC 242) each have a single substantive condition.
- R-009 keeps the payer's stated 90-day filing limit. The evidence alone would allow a threshold as low as 5 days (highest paid claim was submitted at day 4), but lowering it would contradict the documented policy.
- R-022 already spans the full collection range (36400-36416) and the full lab range (80047-89398). The lab condition is the reason for the CARC 97 bundling denial, so it stays.

Every rule is already as general as the evidence safely allows, so I propose no replacements.

- **R-004:** Already a general policy: any line with no diagnosis pointer gets CARC 16.
- **R-012:** 82306 and 82652 are the full vitamin D assay pair, so there is no wider code family. The covered-diagnosis list is the policy itself. Removing it would deny vitamin D tests with covered diagnoses, even though no paid vitamin D claim contradicts that today.
- **R-023:** The E/M range 99202-99215 already covers the office/outpatient family. The 96360-96379 range already covers hydration and injection administration. The injection condition is required, because paid claim CLM-014 is a 99214 without modifier 25 and has no injection. Extending to other procedure families, such as the 11102 biopsy on CLM-040, has no supporting denial.
- **R-024:** I kept the timely-filing exception at days_to_submit > 90. The replay gate would technically accept anything above 5, since the highest denied value is 5. But the only paid evidence is the 262-day claim, and the scrubber only holds claims for timely filing beyond about 90 days. A lower threshold would let this paid prediction fire on ordinary claims without adding real coverage.

No replacements proposed; every rule is already as general as the policy and evidence allow.
- R-013 and R-025 both use CARC 119 but cover different causes. R-013 is the preventive frequency limit (N130) and R-025 is the therapy visit cap (N362), so merging them would be wrong.
- R-021 already lists the full CT/MRI code set. A `between` range from 70450 to 74185 would also catch plain radiographs and other codes outside the prior-auth policy.
- The thresholds in R-005 (180 days), R-013 (365 days) and R-025 (20 visits) match the stated policy limits. The gaps between paid and denied values do not justify moving them.
- R-006 and R-007 have no conditions that can be dropped.
